description:
Almost every office job asks for 'good computer skills'. This course shows you exactly what that means, step by step, on Windows with Microsoft Office.

**Basic stages (free):**
- **Computer basics:** files and folders, clear file names, the shortcuts everyone uses, and staying safe from online scams.

Finish the Basic stages for a free Certificate of Completion.

You follow Bilal, Ayesha and Rashid in Karachi, Lahore and Faisalabad. Menus can differ between Office versions, so we teach the idea and the shortcut, and show you how to find a button that has moved.

Job seekers preparing for office, admin, bank or call-centre roles that test computer skills
Small-business owners who keep records on paper and want simple Excel sheets and charts
Office staff who use Word, Excel and PowerPoint every day but want to work faster and more professionally

sessions.title: Computer Basics: Files, Folders, Shortcuts and Staying Safe Online
sessions.summary: Find any file in seconds with a simple folder plan and clear file names, work faster with the shortcuts every Windows user needs, and spot the scams and risky habits that put your e-mail and money in danger.
objectives: Organise files into folders and name them so they can be found and sorted
Use core Windows shortcuts for copy, paste, undo, save, File Explorer and switching windows
Recognise phishing messages and protect accounts with passphrases and two-step verification

cards.title: The CV that vanished
cards.setting: A small rented room in Gulshan-e-Iqbal, Karachi. Sunday evening. Bilal has a job interview on Tuesday.

lines.text: Welcome to the Office Ready Quest. Your first stop is a laptop that belongs to Bilal, a fresh commerce graduate.
Sana Baji, I typed my CV last week. Now I can't find it anywhere. I think I saved it... somewhere?
Let's look calmly. Did you give it a name, or did you just press Save and close?
I just pressed Save. Also, I got an SMS saying I won a prize and must send my code to claim it. Should I reply?
No reply, no code. We will deal with that too. First, let's learn where files live, so this never happens again.
By the end of today you will find any file in seconds, work faster with shortcuts and spot a scam before it costs you.

scenes.heading: Drives
scenes.narration: Your computer stores everything on a drive. On most Windows laptops the main drive is called C:. A USB stick or an online store such as OneDrive is another place to keep files.

scenes.heading: Folders
scenes.narration: A folder is a labelled box that holds files and other folders. Windows already gives you Documents, Downloads, Desktop and Pictures. You can make your own folders inside them.

scenes.heading: Files
scenes.narration: A file is one piece of work: a letter, a photo, a spreadsheet. Its name has two parts, like CV-Bilal-2026.docx. The part after the dot is the extension, which tells Windows which app opens it.

scenes.heading: The path
scenes.narration: The path is the address of a file, for example Documents > Job Search > CVs. The address bar at the top of File Explorer shows it. If you know the path, you never lose the file.

scenes.heading: Search
scenes.narration: Lost something? Open File Explorer with the Windows key + E, click a folder such as Documents and type part of the file name in the search box. Windows searches that folder and the folders inside it.

cards.title: A simple folder plan for Bilal
cards.caption: Make a few clear folders once, and every new file has an obvious home.

items.label: Documents
items.detail: The main home for your own work. Start here instead of the Desktop.

items.label: Job Search
items.detail: One folder for one area of life. Others could be University, Shop or Personal.

items.label: CVs
items.detail: Inside Job Search, keep each version of your CV.

items.label: Applications
items.detail: A folder for each company, holding the letter and job advert you used.

items.label: Clear file names
items.detail: For example CV-Bilal-Khan-2026-11.docx: who, what and when, with no spaces needed.

cards.title: Good file names save hours
cards.body:
A file name should tell you what is inside without opening it. Use the same pattern every time: **what it is, who or which client, and the date**, for example `Invoice-RashidFabrics-2026-11-03.xlsx`.

- Write dates as year-month-day so files sort in order.
- Avoid names like `new.docx`, `final.docx` and `final-final-2.docx`.
- Do not use these characters, which Windows does not allow: `\ / : * ? " < > |`
- Windows can hide the extension (`.docx`, `.xlsx`, `.pdf`). You can show it from the **View** menu in File Explorer. Where it sits depends on your Windows version.

cards.question: Bilal wants to save his CV so he can find it easily. Which file name is best?
options: CV-Bilal-Khan-2026-11.docx
new document.docx
final final 2.docx
Bilal?CV*.docx
cards.explanation: A clear name says what, who and when. 'new document' and 'final final 2' say nothing, and Windows does not allow the characters ? and * in file names.

cards.back: Copy the selected text, cells or files.
Cut: remove the selection so you can paste it somewhere else.
Paste what you copied or cut.
Undo your last action. Press it again to go back further.
Redo an action you just undid.
Save the file you are working on. Press it often.
Select everything: all the text in a document or all the files in a folder.
Switch between open windows. Keep holding Alt and press Tab to move along.

cards.title: Windows shortcuts for files
cards.prompt: Match each Windows keyboard shortcut to what it does.

pairs.right: Opens File Explorer
Renames the selected file or folder in File Explorer
Creates a new folder in File Explorer
Locks your computer when you step away
Shows the desktop, hiding open windows
Deletes a file without sending it to the Recycle Bin

cards.title: Save vs Save As, and the Recycle Bin
cards.body:
**Save (Ctrl + S)** updates the file you already have. **Save As (F12 in Word, Excel and PowerPoint)** makes a new copy, with a new name or a new place, and leaves the old one as it was.

When you press **Delete** on a file, Windows normally moves it to the **Recycle Bin**, so you can restore it. **Shift + Delete** skips the Recycle Bin, so use it with care. Files deleted from a USB stick or a network folder may not go to the Recycle Bin at all.

cards.title: Safe message or scam?
cards.caption: Scams try to rush you and ask for something secret. Real organisations give you time and never ask for your codes.

items.label: Tone
items.left: Calm, gives you time to check
items.right: Urgent: 'Act in 30 minutes or lose it!'

items.label: Request
items.left: Asks you to log in through the official app or website you already use
items.right: Asks for your one-time code (OTP), PIN or password

items.label: Sender
items.left: Name and address match the real organisation
items.right: Odd spelling, a personal number or a strange e-mail domain

items.label: Offer
items.left: Normal, expected business
items.right: Prizes you never entered, jobs that need a 'fee' first

items.label: Links
items.left: The web address is spelt correctly and you typed it yourself
items.right: Short or misspelt links, files you did not expect

cards.title: Safe habit or risky habit?
cards.prompt: Sort each online habit into the right group.

items.text: Using a long passphrase that is different for every important account
Turning on two-step verification for e-mail and banking
Installing Windows and app updates when they are offered
Typing the bank's web address yourself instead of clicking a link in an SMS
Sharing your OTP with a caller who says he is from your bank
Opening an attachment called invoice.zip from a stranger
Using the same password for e-mail, Facebook and online banking
Downloading cracked software from a random website

cards.title: The prize SMS
cards.situation: Bilal's phone shows: 'Congratulations! Your number has won Rs 50,000 in a lucky draw. Send the 6-digit code you have just received to claim it within 1 hour.' A minute earlier, he got a real-looking code from his mobile wallet app. What should he do?

choices.text: Ignore the message, do not share the code, and report or block the number. If worried, call the wallet's official helpline from its app or website.
choices.outcome: Correct. The 'code' was a real one-time password to take over his wallet. No genuine prize ever needs your OTP. Bilal keeps his money safe.

choices.text: Reply asking for proof that the prize is real before sending anything.
choices.outcome: Replying tells the scammer your number is active, and they may send convincing fake proof. It is safer not to engage at all.

choices.text: Send the code quickly, because the offer ends in an hour.
choices.outcome: The time limit is there to stop you thinking. With the code, the scammer can log in to Bilal's wallet and empty it.

choices.text: Forward the message to friends to ask if anyone else won.
choices.outcome: This spreads the scam and does not protect Bilal. Delete it, do not share the code, and warn friends without forwarding the link.

cards.title: Find and organise a lost file
cards.prompt: Put Bilal's steps in the right order to find his CV and store it properly.
steps: Press Windows key + E to open File Explorer
Click Documents, then type 'CV' in the search box
Open the file to check it is the right CV
Close it, then right-click in Documents and choose New > Folder
Name the new folder 'Job Search' and press Enter
Drag the CV into the folder and rename it with F2

cards.title: Rashid's shop folders
cards.body:
Rashid Bhatti runs a fabric shop in Faisalabad. His invoices used to sit on the Desktop with names like `bill1`, `bill2` and `new bill`. Now he has one folder, **Rashid Fabrics**, with **Invoices**, **Suppliers**, **Staff** and **Photos** inside. Each month he makes a folder such as `2026-11`.

When a supplier asked about an invoice from March, Rashid opened `Invoices > 2026-03` and found it in under a minute. He also keeps a copy of the whole folder on OneDrive, so a broken laptop does not mean lost records.

cards.question: Which of these is the strongest protection for Bilal's e-mail account?
options: His date of birth, because it is easy to remember
A long, unique passphrase plus two-step verification
A short password he also uses on his other accounts
Writing his password on a note stuck to the screen
cards.explanation: A long, unique passphrase is hard to guess, and two-step verification stops someone who learns the password. Dates of birth and reused passwords are the first things attackers try.

cards.title: Take-aways from the Desktop Gate
items: Files live in folders on a drive. The path, such as Documents > Job Search > CVs, is the file's address.
Name files with what, who and when, and write dates as year-month-day so they sort in order.
Core shortcuts: Ctrl+C copy, Ctrl+X cut, Ctrl+V paste, Ctrl+Z undo, Ctrl+S save, Windows key+E File Explorer.
Delete sends files to the Recycle Bin; Shift+Delete skips it, so use it with care.
Never share an OTP, PIN or password. Urgency, prizes and odd links are warning signs of a scam.
Use long, unique passphrases, turn on two-step verification and install updates.

cards.prompt: Open your own Documents or Desktop folder. Which three files would be hard to find next month? Write down the folder plan and file names you will use for them from today.

quiz.question: What does the part of a file name after the dot, such as .xlsx, tell Windows?
options: How large the file is and the date and time it was last saved
Which folder the file is stored in on the drive
Who created the file and who may edit it
Which type of file it is and which app should open it
quiz.explanation: The extension shows the file type. .docx opens in Word, .xlsx in Excel, .pptx in PowerPoint and .pdf in a PDF reader.

quiz.question: Which keyboard shortcut opens File Explorer in Windows?
options: Windows key + D
Windows key + E
Ctrl + Shift + E
Alt + F4
quiz.explanation: Windows key + E opens File Explorer. Windows key + D shows the desktop, and Alt + F4 closes the active window.

quiz.question: Ayesha deleted the wrong file by pressing Delete in her laptop's Documents folder. Where should she look first?
options: The Downloads folder, where deleted files go
Nowhere, because deleted files are gone for good
The Recycle Bin, where she can restore it
The Control Panel's file history page
quiz.explanation: On the laptop's own drive, Delete normally moves files to the Recycle Bin. Right-click the file there and choose Restore.

quiz.question: Which shortcut undoes your last action in most Windows programs?
options: Ctrl + Z
Ctrl + Y
Shift + Delete
Ctrl + X
quiz.explanation: Ctrl + Z undoes. Ctrl + Y redoes, Ctrl + X cuts, and Shift + Delete deletes a file without using the Recycle Bin.

quiz.question: Rashid wants to rename a file he has selected in File Explorer. Which key does this directly?
options: F5
F2
F7
quiz.explanation: F2 renames the selected item in File Explorer. F5 refreshes the view; F12 is Save As in Office apps and F7 is spelling in Word.

quiz.question: Why is it a good idea to write dates in file names as 2026-11-03 instead of 3-11-26?
options: Files then sort in the right date order by name
Windows does not allow day-first dates in names
It makes the file smaller and faster to open
Office apps need the year first to open the file
quiz.explanation: Year-month-day puts the biggest unit first, so an alphabetical sort is also a date sort. Day-first dates are allowed but sort out of order.

quiz.question: A caller says he is from your bank and needs the code just sent to your phone to 'stop a fraud'. What is the right response?
options: Hang up and call the bank's official helpline yourself
Read out the code so he can block the fraud
Give only the first three digits of the code, to be safe and quick
Ask him to confirm your name and then share it
quiz.explanation: Banks do not ask for your one-time code. Scammers often already know your name. End the call and contact the bank using a number you find yourself.

quiz.question: What is the difference between Save and Save As?
options: Save As works only for PDF files; Save works for all files
Save As creates a copy with a new name or place; Save updates the current file
Save keeps a backup copy; Save As deletes the older version
Save sends the file to OneDrive; Save As keeps it only on the laptop's own drive
quiz.explanation: Save (Ctrl + S) updates the file you have open. Save As (F12 in Office) makes a new file and leaves the original unchanged.

quiz.question: Which of these is the safest way to visit your bank's website?
options: Type the address yourself or use the bank's official app
Click the link in an SMS that says your account is locked
Search for the bank and click the first advert shown
Use a link a friend forwarded on a messaging group
quiz.explanation: Links in messages and even adverts can lead to fake sites. Typing the correct address or using the official app avoids them.

quiz.question: Bilal holds Alt and presses Tab. What happens?
options: His computer locks until he signs in again
He moves between his open windows
The active window closes without saving
All windows minimise to show the desktop
quiz.explanation: Alt + Tab switches between open windows. Windows key + L locks, Alt + F4 closes the window, and Windows key + D shows the desktop.

sessions.title: Microsoft Word Basics: Typing, Formatting and a Professional Letter and CV
sessions.summary: Find your way around Word, type and format the proper way so layouts never break, and produce a clean one-page CV and a professional cover letter saved as a PDF.
objectives: Navigate the Ribbon and use the search box to find any command
Format text and paragraphs with shortcuts, alignment, page breaks and hidden marks
Write and lay out a professional cover letter and a one-page CV, and save them as PDF

cards.title: Five fonts and a rainbow
cards.setting: Ayesha's study table in Johar Town, Lahore. A job advert for a trainee at a Lahore software house closes on Friday.

lines.text: Sana Baji, look at my CV! I used five fonts, three colours and a picture of a flower in the corner.
You have worked hard. Now imagine an HR officer reading two hundred CVs before lunch. What will they look for?
My name, my degree, my skills... quickly, I suppose.
Exactly. Clean beats colourful. One or two fonts, clear headings, and everything lined up neatly.
I also pressed Enter at the end of every line and used spaces to move my dates to the right. Is that bad?
That is why things jump around when you change one word. Today we will fix it the proper Word way, and write your cover letter too.

scenes.heading: The Ribbon
scenes.narration: The strip of buttons at the top is the Ribbon. It is split into tabs: Home for fonts and paragraphs, Insert for pictures and tables, Layout for margins, and more. Click a tab to see its buttons.

scenes.heading: The search box
scenes.narration: Not sure where a button is? Type what you want, such as 'page number', into the search box at the top of Word. Button positions differ between versions, but search finds them.

scenes.heading: The page
scenes.narration: The white page is where you type. Word wraps text to the next line by itself, so press Enter only when you want a new paragraph.

scenes.heading: The status bar
scenes.narration: The bar at the bottom shows the page number, word count and zoom slider. Click the word count to see more detail.

scenes.heading: Saving
scenes.narration: Press Ctrl + S often. The first time, Word asks for a name and a folder. Use your folder plan from the last stage.

cards.title: Type it right the first time
cards.body:
A few habits make every document neat and easy to change:

- **Let the text wrap.** Press Enter only at the end of a paragraph.
- **Do not use spaces to line things up.** Use alignment (Ctrl + L left, Ctrl + E centre, Ctrl + R right, Ctrl + J justify) or a Tab stop.
- **Use a page break, not lots of Enters,** to start a new page: Ctrl + Enter.
- **Show the hidden marks** with Ctrl + Shift + 8 (the ¶ button on the Home tab) to see spaces, tabs and paragraph marks. Press it again to hide them.
- **Check spelling** with F7, but still read it yourself. A spell checker will not notice 'form' typed instead of 'from'.

cards.back: Bold the selected text.
Italic.
Underline.
Centre the paragraph.
Align the paragraph left or right.
Insert a page break and start a new page.
Show or hide paragraph marks and other hidden formatting symbols.
Check spelling and grammar.

cards.question: Ayesha wants her name centred at the top of her CV. She selects it. Which shortcut centres it?
options: Ctrl + C
Ctrl + Shift + C
Ctrl + E
Ctrl + M
cards.explanation: Ctrl + E centres a paragraph in Word. Ctrl + C copies. Remember E for 'cEntre' because C was already taken by Copy.

cards.title: A CV that confuses vs a CV that gets read
cards.caption: Recruiters often scan a CV in under a minute. Make the important things easy to see.

items.label: Fonts
items.left: Five fonts, some decorative
items.right: One clear font such as Calibri or Arial, size 10.5 to 12

items.label: Headings
items.left: Random bold and underline
items.right: The same style for every heading: Education, Experience, Skills

items.label: Layout
items.left: Spaces and Enters to push text around
items.right: Alignment, tabs or a simple table without borders

items.label: Length
items.left: Four pages of everything
items.right: One page for a fresh graduate, two at most

items.label: Details
items.left: CNIC number, family income, a casual selfie
items.right: Name, phone, e-mail, city, and a LinkedIn link if you have one

cards.title: Parts of a professional letter
cards.caption: A cover letter or business letter follows the same simple order. Keep it to one page.

items.label: Your details
items.detail: Name, phone, e-mail and city at the top.

items.label: Date
items.detail: Write it in full, for example 25 November 2026, so nobody misreads it.

items.label: Recipient
items.detail: The person's name, title, company and city.

items.label: Subject line
items.detail: For example: Application for Trainee Software Tester (Ref: TST-11).

items.label: Greeting
items.detail: 'Dear Ms Farah' if you know the name; 'Dear Hiring Manager' if you do not.

items.label: Body
items.detail: Three short paragraphs: why you are writing, why you fit, what you would like to happen next.

items.label: Closing and name
items.detail: 'Yours sincerely' when you used a name; 'Yours faithfully' with 'Dear Sir or Madam'. Then your full name.

cards.title: Keep it on the CV or leave it off?
cards.prompt: Sort each item for a fresh graduate's one-page CV.

items.text: Phone number and a professional e-mail address
Degree, university and year of graduation
Internship or part-time work, with one result each
Computer skills such as Word, Excel and PowerPoint
CNIC number and bank account details
An e-mail address like cutepari786@...
A list of every school prize since Class 3
The same sentence written in three different fonts

cards.title: Which Word tool do you need?
cards.prompt: Match each task to the Word feature that does it.

pairs.left: Make the CV one page by shrinking the page edges
pairs.right: Layout tab > Margins

pairs.left: Put a neat line of bullets under Skills
pairs.right: Home tab > Bullets

pairs.left: Change 'Lahore Colege' everywhere in one go
pairs.right: Find and Replace (Ctrl + H)

pairs.left: Copy the look of one heading onto another
pairs.right: Format Painter on the Home tab

pairs.left: Send the CV in a form that looks the same on any device
pairs.right: Save As, choosing PDF as the file type

cards.title: The letter that will not stay straight
cards.situation: Ayesha's cover letter looks fine until she adds one word to the first line. Suddenly her address moves, her date jumps to the next line and a big gap appears. She has one hour before she wants to e-mail it. What should she do?

choices.text: Press Ctrl + Shift + 8 to show the hidden marks, remove the extra spaces and Enters, and use right alignment and a single paragraph per block.
choices.outcome: The marks show dozens of spaces and line-end Enters. After cleaning them up, the letter stays neat whatever she types. It takes fifteen minutes and saves her every time.

choices.text: Delete the new word so the layout goes back to how it was.
choices.outcome: The layout is fixed for now, but the problem is still hidden. The next change will break it again.

choices.text: Retype the whole letter in a new document.
choices.outcome: This takes longer and, if she uses the same habits, the same thing will happen again.

choices.text: Take a screenshot of the letter and send the picture instead.
choices.outcome: Recruiters cannot copy or search a picture, and it looks unprofessional. Always send a proper document or PDF.

cards.title: Ayesha's cover letter, first paragraph
cards.body:
Here is how Ayesha opens her letter, in her own words:

> Dear Ms Farah,
>
> I am writing to apply for the Trainee Software Tester role advertised on your company's careers page. I have just completed my BS in Computer Science at a university in Lahore, where I tested our final-year attendance app with 40 classmates and fixed 23 reported problems.

It is short, names the job, and gives one real result with a number. The rest of the letter explains why she fits and asks politely for an interview.

cards.title: Save your CV as a PDF
cards.prompt: Put the steps in order to send a CV that looks the same on every phone and computer.
steps: Finish the CV and press F7 to check spelling
Read it once more yourself, slowly, out loud
Press F12 (Save As) or go to File > Save As
Choose the Job Search > CVs folder
In 'Save as type', choose PDF
Give it a clear name such as CV-Ayesha-Malik-2026.pdf and click Save

cards.question: Ayesha does not know the hiring manager's name. Which greeting and closing go together correctly in formal British-style English?
options: 'Dear Sir or Madam' ... 'Yours sincerely'
'Hi there' ... 'Cheers'
'Respected Sir' ... 'Best of luck'
'Dear Sir or Madam' ... 'Yours faithfully'
cards.explanation: In formal British-style letters, 'Yours faithfully' goes with an unnamed reader and 'Yours sincerely' with a named one. Many employers now accept 'Dear Hiring Manager' with 'Yours sincerely' too.

cards.title: A clean CV in Word, quickly
cards.body:
Start from a **simple template** (File > New, then search 'CV' or 'resume'), or a blank page with one font. Use **bold** for headings and job titles only. Line up dates with a **right-aligned Tab stop** or a **table with no borders**.

Menus and button names can differ between Office versions (for example Microsoft 365, Office 2021 or Office 2016), so if a button has moved, use the search box at the top of the window.

cards.title: Take-aways from the Writing Desk
items: The Ribbon groups tools into tabs; if you cannot find a button, use the search box at the top.
Let text wrap, press Enter only for a new paragraph, and use Ctrl + Enter for a new page.
Use alignment and tabs, not spaces, and show hidden marks with Ctrl + Shift + 8 to fix messy layouts.
A strong CV is one page, one font, clear headings and real results with numbers. Leave off CNIC and bank details.
A professional letter has your details, date, recipient, subject, greeting, three short paragraphs and a matching closing.
Check spelling with F7, read it yourself, then save as a PDF with a clear file name.

cards.prompt: Open your own CV, or start one. Show hidden marks with Ctrl + Shift + 8. What would a recruiter notice first, and which two changes will make it cleaner today?

quiz.question: In Word, which shortcut makes the selected text bold?
options: Ctrl + D
Ctrl + Shift + B
Ctrl + B
Alt + B
quiz.explanation: Ctrl + B applies bold. Ctrl + I is italic and Ctrl + U is underline.

quiz.question: Ayesha wants the next part of her document to start on a new page. What is the best way?
options: Press Enter many times until a new page appears
Press Tab until the cursor jumps to the next page
Open a new document and copy the text into it
Press Ctrl + Enter to insert a page break
quiz.explanation: A page break (Ctrl + Enter) always starts a new page, even if you later add or remove text above it. Many Enters will shift as the text changes.

quiz.question: What does Ctrl + Shift + 8 do in Word for Windows?
options: Inserts a bulleted list at the cursor
Makes the selected text eight points larger than before
Shows or hides paragraph marks, spaces and tabs
Opens the spelling and grammar checker
quiz.explanation: Ctrl + Shift + 8 toggles the ¶ symbols so you can see hidden formatting such as extra spaces and Enters.

quiz.question: Which key starts the spelling and grammar check in Word?
options: F5
Shift + F7
F1
F7
quiz.explanation: F7 starts the spelling and grammar check (shown as Editor in newer versions). Shift + F7 opens the Thesaurus and F1 opens help.

quiz.question: Why should you use alignment or tab stops instead of spaces to line up text?
options: Word removes extra spaces automatically when you save
Spaces make the file much larger and slower to open
Spaces move when text changes, so the layout breaks easily
Recruiters' screening software deletes every extra space from CVs
quiz.explanation: Spaces depend on the width of each letter, so adding one word pushes everything along. Alignment and tabs keep positions fixed.

quiz.question: A fresh graduate is writing a CV. Which is the best length?
options: One page, two at the most
Three to four pages to show everything
Exactly half a page, whatever the experience
As long as needed, with every school certificate
quiz.explanation: Recruiters scan quickly. For someone early in their career, one focused page is usually best.

quiz.question: Ayesha writes 'Dear Ms Farah' at the start of her letter. Which closing matches it in formal British-style English?
options: Yours faithfully
Yours lovingly
Best of luck
Yours sincerely
quiz.explanation: Use 'Yours sincerely' when you name the reader, and 'Yours faithfully' with 'Dear Sir or Madam'.

quiz.question: Which Word feature copies the formatting of one heading and applies it to another?
options: Format Painter
Find and Replace
Track Changes
Word Count
quiz.explanation: Format Painter (the paintbrush on the Home tab) copies fonts, size and colour from one place to another.

quiz.question: Why do many employers prefer a CV sent as a PDF?
options: It can be edited more easily by the recruiter
It is always accepted by every website without checks
It looks the same on any phone or computer
It hides spelling mistakes from the reader
quiz.explanation: A PDF keeps fonts and layout the same on different devices. Some online forms ask for Word files instead, so always follow the instructions in the advert.

quiz.question: Which shortcut opens Find and Replace in Word, so you can fix a misspelt word everywhere at once?
options: Ctrl + R
Ctrl + G
Ctrl + Shift + F
Ctrl + H
quiz.explanation: Ctrl + H opens the Replace tab. Ctrl + R right-aligns, Ctrl + G opens Go To, and Ctrl + Shift + F opens the Font dialog.

sessions.title: Excel and PowerPoint Basics: Cells, Simple Formulas, a Chart and a 5-Slide Talk
sessions.summary: Turn a hand-written sales notebook into an Excel sheet with SUM and AVERAGE, draw a clear chart, and build a clean five-slide presentation with one idea per slide.
objectives: Read cell references and ranges and enter data that formulas can use
Use SUM, AVERAGE, MIN, MAX and COUNT, and check formulas in the formula bar
Choose and create a suitable chart
Build a clean five-slide presentation and run it

cards.title: The calculator and the notebook
cards.setting: Rashid Fabrics, a busy cloth shop in Faisalabad. Saturday night, after closing.

lines.text: Every night I add up the day's sales on a calculator and write them in this notebook. Last month the total was wrong by eleven thousand rupees.
Uncle, one wrong key on the calculator and the whole month is wrong. Excel can add it for you, and check itself.
Excel looks like a giant empty table. I would not know where to start.
That empty table is your new notebook, Rashid Sahib. Today, one sheet, one SUM, one chart. That is all.
And my supplier wants a short presentation about my new lawn collection. Can Ayesha help with that too?
Five clean slides. You will be surprised how little you need to say when the chart says it for you.

scenes.heading: Cells
scenes.narration: A worksheet is a grid. Columns have letters (A, B, C) and rows have numbers (1, 2, 3). Each box is a cell, named by its column and row: B3 is column B, row 3.

scenes.heading: Ranges
scenes.narration: A range is a block of cells. B2:B8 means every cell from B2 down to B8. The colon means 'to'.

scenes.heading: Formulas
scenes.narration: A formula always starts with an equals sign. Type =B2+B3 and Excel adds those two cells. Change a number and the answer updates at once.

scenes.heading: Functions
scenes.narration: Functions are ready-made formulas. =SUM(B2:B8) adds the whole range. =AVERAGE(B2:B8) finds the average. You do not need a calculator.

scenes.heading: Charts
scenes.narration: Select your labels and numbers, then insert a chart. Excel draws it for you, and it updates when the numbers change.

cards.title: A typed total vs a formula
cards.caption: If you type the answer yourself, Excel cannot check it or update it. Let a formula do the work.

items.label: What you type in B9
items.right: =SUM(B2:B8)

items.label: If a sale is corrected
items.left: The total stays wrong until you notice
items.right: The total updates by itself

items.label: Checking
items.left: You must add it all again
items.right: Click the cell to see exactly what is added

items.label: Copying to next month
items.left: Retype every total
items.right: Copy the formula across, and it adjusts

cards.back: Adds all the numbers in B2 to B8.
Adds them and divides by how many numbers there are.
Finds the smallest number, such as the slowest day.
Finds the largest number, such as the best day.
Counts how many cells contain numbers.
AutoSum: inserts a SUM formula for the numbers above or to the left. Check the range, then press Enter.

cards.question: Rashid's sales for four days are in B2:B5: 100, 200, 300 and 400 (in thousands of rupees). What does =AVERAGE(B2:B5) show?
cards.explanation: AVERAGE adds the four numbers (1000) and divides by four, giving 250. SUM would show 1000, MAX 400 and MIN 100.

cards.title: Moving around and fixing mistakes
cards.body:
- **Enter** moves down one cell; **Tab** moves right.
- **F2** lets you edit the cell you are in without retyping it.
- **Ctrl + Home** jumps back to cell A1.
- **Ctrl + Z** undoes, just like in Word.
- If a cell shows **#####**, the column is too narrow to show the number. Double-click the line between the column letters to widen it.
- Do not type 'Rs' or commas into number cells. Type `12500`, then format the cells as numbers or currency (Ctrl + 1 opens Format Cells). Then formulas can use them.

cards.title: Read the formula
cards.prompt: Cells B2:B6 hold 4, 10, 16, 20 and 50. Match each formula to its result.

pairs.right: 50, the largest value
4, the smallest value
5, because five cells contain numbers

cards.title: Make your first chart
cards.caption: The same steps work for most charts. Names of buttons can differ between versions.

items.label: Select the data
items.detail: Drag over the day names and the sales numbers, including the headings.

items.label: Insert a chart
items.detail: Go to Insert > Recommended Charts, or press Alt + F1 for a quick chart on the same sheet.

items.label: Pick the right type
items.detail: Column chart to compare days; line chart for a trend over months.

items.label: Add a clear title
items.detail: Click the chart title and type, for example, 'Daily sales, week of 3 Nov (Rs 000)'.

items.label: Tidy it
items.detail: Remove anything you do not need and keep the colours simple.

cards.title: Which chart fits?
cards.prompt: Choose the clearest chart type for each of Rashid's questions.

items.text: Which day of last week had the most sales?
Compare sales of lawn, cotton and silk this month
How have monthly sales changed over the last 12 months?
Is the number of customers per week going up or down this year?
What share of this month's sales came from each of three fabric types?
How is one day's takings split between cash, card and mobile wallet?

cards.title: The total that did not change
cards.situation: Rashid corrects Tuesday's sales in B4 from 18,000 to 21,000. But the weekly total in B9 still says 125,400. He clicks B9 and the formula bar shows 125400, not a formula. What should he do?

choices.text: Replace the typed number with =SUM(B2:B8), press Enter, and check that the formula bar now shows the formula.
choices.outcome: The total becomes 128,400 and will update every time a sale changes. Rashid now knows to look in the formula bar to check.

choices.text: Add 3,000 to the total by hand.
choices.outcome: The number is right today, but the next correction will make it wrong again. Typed totals do not update.

choices.text: Delete the whole sheet and start again tomorrow.
choices.outcome: Nothing was wrong with the sheet except one typed number. Starting again wastes the whole week's work.

choices.text: Use a calculator to recheck the whole week.
choices.outcome: It might find the right total, but it brings back the very problem Excel was meant to solve.

cards.title: A clean 5-slide presentation
cards.prompt: Put Rashid's five slides for his supplier meeting in a sensible order.
steps: Title: 'New Lawn Collection: Spring Order Plan', with his name and date
The situation: what customers asked for last season, in three short points
The numbers: one column chart of last season's sales by design
The plan: which designs and quantities he wants to order
Next steps: delivery dates, who does what, and a thank you

cards.title: Slide 3, before and after
cards.body:
**Before:** a slide with the heading 'Sales', a full table of 40 numbers copied from Excel, and six bullet points underneath in small text.

**After:** the heading 'Floral designs sold out first'. One column chart showing sales by design, with the top two bars in a stronger colour. One short line below: 'Floral 1 and 2 sold out in three weeks.'

The second slide tells the supplier the point in five seconds. Rashid explains the details out loud.

cards.question: In PowerPoint, which shortcut adds a new slide?
options: Ctrl + N
Ctrl + M
Ctrl + S
Ctrl + D
cards.explanation: Ctrl + M inserts a new slide. Ctrl + N creates a whole new presentation, and Ctrl + D duplicates the selected slide or object.

cards.title: Slide basics that always work
cards.body:
- Start PowerPoint, choose a simple **design theme** from the Design tab and keep it for every slide.
- Use the ready-made **layouts** (Home > Layout) so titles and text line up.
- Aim for one idea per slide, a heading that says the point, and large text.
- Press **F5** to start the show from the first slide and **Esc** to end it.

Menus and button names can differ between Office versions (for example Microsoft 365, Office 2021 or Office 2016), so if a button has moved, use the search box at the top of the window.

cards.title: Take-aways from the Market Ledger
items: Cells are named by column letter and row number (B3); a range such as B2:B8 means from B2 to B8.
Every formula starts with =. Use =SUM, =AVERAGE, =MIN, =MAX and =COUNT instead of a calculator.
Never type a total by hand; check the formula bar to see whether a cell holds a formula.
Column charts compare items, line charts show change over time, pie charts show parts of one whole.
A clean 5-slide talk: title, situation, numbers, plan, next steps. One idea and one clear heading per slide.
In PowerPoint, Ctrl + M adds a slide, F5 starts the show and Esc ends it.

cards.prompt: Think of numbers you track by hand: pocket money, shop sales, bills or study hours. Which column headings would your first Excel sheet have, and which chart would show the most useful picture?

quiz.question: What does the cell reference C7 mean in Excel?
options: Row C, column 7
Column C, row 7
The seventh sheet in the file
Seven cells starting from column C
quiz.explanation: Cells are named by column letter first, then row number.

quiz.question: Which of these is a correctly written Excel formula to add the cells B2 to B10?
options: SUM B2 to B10
=SUM(B2:B10)
=ADD(B2-B10)
+TOTAL(B2;B10)
quiz.explanation: Formulas start with =, SUM is the function name, and a colon marks a range.

quiz.question: Cells A1:A4 hold 10, 20, 30 and 40. What does =MAX(A1:A4) return?
quiz.explanation: MAX returns the largest value. SUM would give 100, AVERAGE 25 and MIN 10.

quiz.question: A cell shows ##### instead of a number. What is the most likely cause?
options: The column is too narrow to show the number
The formula has a spelling mistake in the function name
The file has been damaged
The number is negative and hidden
quiz.explanation: Widen the column (double-click the right edge of the column letter) and the number appears.

quiz.question: Which keyboard shortcut inserts an AutoSum formula in Excel?
options: Ctrl + =
Shift + S
Alt + =
Ctrl + Alt + S
quiz.explanation: Alt + = inserts =SUM() for the nearby numbers. Always check the range Excel guesses before pressing Enter.

quiz.question: Rashid wants to show how monthly sales changed over a year. Which chart type is usually clearest?
options: A pie chart
A doughnut chart
A line chart
A table of 12 numbers on a slide
quiz.explanation: Line charts show trends over time well. Pie charts show parts of one whole and get hard to read with many slices.

quiz.question: Rashid clicks the weekly total cell and the formula bar shows 125400 with no = sign. What does this tell him?
options: The SUM formula is working correctly
Excel has hidden the formula to protect it from accidental changes
The cell is formatted as currency
The total was typed in and will not update by itself
quiz.explanation: A formula shows in the formula bar starting with =. A plain number means someone typed it, so it will not change when the sales change.

quiz.question: Which shortcut starts a PowerPoint slide show from the first slide?
options: F7
Ctrl + F5
F5
Ctrl + P
quiz.explanation: F5 starts from the beginning. Shift + F5 starts from the current slide. F7 checks spelling.

quiz.question: Why should you type 12500 rather than 'Rs 12,500' into a sales cell?
options: Excel treats typed 'Rs' text as words, so formulas may not count it
Excel cannot show the rupee symbol or commas in any cell, however it is set up
Commas in numbers make the file too large to save
Typing 'Rs' changes the cell into a date
quiz.explanation: Type the plain number and use number or currency formatting (Ctrl + 1) to show 'Rs' and commas. Text with 'Rs' in front may be ignored by SUM.

quiz.question: Which slide heading follows the 'one idea per slide' rule best?
options: Sales
Information
Floral designs sold out first
Sales figures and other information
quiz.explanation: A heading that states the point tells the audience what to notice. 'Sales' or 'Information' only names a topic.

sessions.title: Advanced Word: Styles, Tables, Mail Merge and Track Changes
sessions.summary: Produce long, consistent documents with styles and an automatic table of contents, build tables that behave, send hundreds of personal letters with mail merge, and review safely with Track Changes and comments.
objectives: Use and modify heading styles and generate an automatic table of contents
Create and manage tables, including repeating header rows
Run a letter mail merge from an Excel list and check the results
Review documents with Track Changes and comments, and clean them before sharing

cards.title: Twenty pages and 150 letters
cards.setting: Bilal's first month as office assistant at a logistics company on Shahrah-e-Faisal, Karachi.

lines.text: My manager wants a 20-page training report with a contents page by Thursday. And invitation letters to 150 clients, each with their own name.
Congratulations on the job! Two big tasks, two Word features: styles for the report, mail merge for the letters.
I was going to type 150 letters by hand...
That would take days and one wrong name could embarrass the company. Mail merge does it in minutes from one Excel list.
Also, my manager will edit the report. Last time she rewrote things and I could not see what she changed.
Then you will turn on Track Changes. Welcome to the Advanced stages, where Word becomes a real office tool.

cards.title: Styles: the secret of long documents

scenes.heading: What a style is
scenes.narration: A style is a saved set of formatting with a name, such as Heading 1, Heading 2 or Normal. Apply it with one click from the Home tab, or with Ctrl + Alt + 1 for Heading 1 and Ctrl + Alt + 2 for Heading 2.

scenes.heading: Change once, update everywhere
scenes.narration: Want all main headings blue and size 16? Right-click Heading 1 in the Styles gallery and choose Modify. Every Heading 1 in the report changes at once.

scenes.heading: The Navigation Pane
scenes.narration: Headings appear in the Navigation Pane (View > Navigation Pane, or Ctrl + F). Click a heading to jump to it, or drag it to move a whole section.

scenes.heading: Automatic contents
scenes.narration: Go to References > Table of Contents and choose a built-in style. Word lists every heading with its page number. After edits, click Update Table.

scenes.heading: Page numbers
scenes.narration: Insert > Page Number adds numbers in the header or footer that stay correct as pages are added.

cards.title: Manual formatting vs styles
cards.caption: For a one-page note, manual formatting is fine. For a report, styles save hours and avoid mistakes.

items.label: Making a heading
items.left: Select, bold, change size, change colour, every time
items.right: Click Heading 1 once

items.label: Changing the look
items.left: Fix all 40 headings one by one
items.right: Modify the style once

items.label: Contents page
items.left: Type it by hand; page numbers go out of date
items.right: References > Table of Contents, then Update Table

items.label: Moving a section
items.left: Cut and paste, hoping nothing is lost
items.right: Drag the heading in the Navigation Pane

cards.question: Bilal has applied Heading 1 to 12 chapter titles. His manager wants all of them dark green. What is the fastest correct method?
options: Select each title in turn and change its colour
Use Find and Replace to search for each title
Modify the Heading 1 style so every chapter title updates at once
Retype the titles in green text
cards.explanation: Modifying the style changes every paragraph that uses it, so the document stays consistent and it takes seconds.

cards.back: Insert > Table, then drag over the grid to choose rows and columns.
Click in the last cell and press Tab. Word adds a new row.
Select the top row, then in Table Layout choose Repeat Header Rows, so it shows on every page.
Select cells and choose Merge Cells in Table Layout to make one wide cell.
Table Layout > Sort puts rows in order, for example by client name.
Apply a ready-made look with banded rows. Choose a light design for easy reading.

cards.title: How mail merge works
cards.caption: One letter, one list, many personal copies. On the Mailings tab the buttons follow this order.

items.label: Prepare the list
items.detail: An Excel sheet with headings in row 1: Title, FirstName, LastName, Company, City.

items.label: Start Mail Merge
items.detail: Mailings > Start Mail Merge > Letters.

items.label: Select Recipients
items.detail: Choose Use an Existing List and pick the Excel file and sheet.

items.label: Insert Merge Fields
items.detail: Place fields such as «FirstName» and «Company» where each person's details go.

items.label: Preview Results
items.detail: Click through several letters to check names, spaces and punctuation.

items.label: Finish & Merge
items.detail: Edit Individual Documents to check them all, then print or save as PDF.

cards.title: Bilal's mail merge, step by step
cards.prompt: Put the steps in the right order.
steps: Check the Excel client list: one row per client, headings in row 1, no blank rows
Write the invitation letter in Word, leaving gaps for the personal details
Mailings > Start Mail Merge > Letters, then Select Recipients > Use an Existing List
Insert Merge Fields for the title, name and company in the right places
Preview Results and check at least five letters, including long names
Finish & Merge > Edit Individual Documents, then save or print

cards.title: Track Changes and comments
cards.body:
When someone else will edit your document, turn on **Review > Track Changes** (shortcut **Ctrl + Shift + E**). Every insertion, deletion and formatting change is recorded with the editor's name.

- **Comments** (Review > New Comment, or **Ctrl + Alt + M**) ask a question without changing the text.
- **Accept** or **Reject** each change with the buttons on the Review tab, or accept all at once when you are sure.
- The **Display for Review** list switches between Simple Markup, All Markup, No Markup and Original. **No Markup only hides changes; it does not remove them.**
- Before sending a final version outside the company, accept or reject every change, delete comments, and use **File > Info > Check for Issues > Inspect Document**.

cards.title: Track Changes vocabulary
cards.prompt: Match each Review tab term to its meaning.

pairs.right: Records every edit, showing who made it
Keeps an edit and makes it part of the normal text
Removes an edit and restores what was there before
Adds a note or question in the margin without changing the text
Shows the document as if changes were accepted, but keeps them hidden in the file
Finds hidden comments, tracked changes and personal details before sharing

cards.title: The contract with secret edits
cards.situation: Bilal's manager asks him to e-mail a service agreement to a client. He sets the view to No Markup, the document looks clean and he is about to attach it. In the file there are still tracked changes, including a deleted line where the company had considered a lower price, and a comment saying 'Can we push them higher?'. What should he do?

choices.text: Stop. Ask the manager which changes are final, accept or reject them all, delete the comments, run Inspect Document and send a PDF.
choices.outcome: Exactly right. The client receives only the agreed text. Bilal has protected the company's negotiating position and his own reputation.

choices.text: Send it, because No Markup shows a clean document.
choices.outcome: No Markup only hides the changes on Bilal's screen. The client can switch to All Markup and read the deleted price and the comment.

choices.text: Accept all changes and send it straight away.
choices.outcome: This removes the tracking, but the comments may remain, and the manager has not confirmed that every change is final.

choices.text: Turn off Track Changes and send it.
choices.outcome: Turning off Track Changes stops recording new edits. It does not remove the edits and comments already in the file.

cards.title: Styles, table or mail merge?
cards.prompt: Choose the best Word feature for each task.

items.text: Make all 30 section headings look the same and appear in the contents page
Change the font of every heading in a 40-page report in one step
Line up a price list with item, size and price columns
Show a staff duty roster for each day of the week
Send personal certificates to 80 workshop participants
Print address labels for 200 customers from an Excel list

cards.title: Small habits of professional documents
cards.body:
- Use **Layout > Breaks > Next Page** when one part needs a different page orientation, such as a wide table.
- Insert captions under tables and pictures (References > Insert Caption) so they number themselves.
- Keep a copy of your mail merge Excel list in the same folder as the letter. If you move one, Word may ask where the other one went.

Menus and button names can differ between Office versions (for example Microsoft 365, Office 2021 or Office 2016), so if a button has moved, use the search box at the top of the window.

cards.question: After his manager's edits, Bilal turns off Track Changes. What happens to the edits she already made?
options: They are all accepted automatically
They are all removed from the document
They turn into comments in the margin
They stay in the document until someone accepts or rejects them
cards.explanation: Turning off Track Changes only stops recording new edits. Existing changes remain until they are accepted or rejected.

cards.title: Take-aways from the Print House
items: Use built-in styles (Heading 1, Heading 2, Normal); modify a style once to change every matching paragraph.
Styled headings power the Navigation Pane and an automatic table of contents that you refresh with Update Table.
In tables, press Tab in the last cell to add a row, and use Repeat Header Rows for long tables.
Mail merge: prepare the Excel list, Start Mail Merge, Select Recipients, Insert Merge Fields, Preview Results, Finish & Merge.
Track Changes (Ctrl + Shift + E) records edits; No Markup only hides them, and turning tracking off does not remove them.
Before sharing outside, accept or reject all changes, delete comments and run Inspect Document.

cards.prompt: Which long or repeated document at your study or work could be built faster with styles or mail merge? Sketch the headings or the Excel columns you would need.

quiz.question: Which shortcut applies the Heading 1 style in Word for Windows?
options: Ctrl + 1
Ctrl + Alt + 1
Alt + H + 1
Ctrl + Shift + H
quiz.explanation: Ctrl + Alt + 1 applies Heading 1 and Ctrl + Alt + 2 applies Heading 2. Ctrl + 1 sets single line spacing in Word.

quiz.question: Bilal adds two new chapters to his report. What must he do to make the table of contents show them?
options: Delete the old table and type a new one by hand with the new pages
Save the file; Word updates it on every save
Nothing; it always updates instantly while typing
Click the table of contents and choose Update Table
quiz.explanation: A Word table of contents is updated on request. Use Update Table and choose to update the entire table.

quiz.question: In a Word table, what happens when you press Tab in the very last cell?
options: The cursor leaves the table
A new row is added
A tab space is typed in the cell
The table is deleted
quiz.explanation: Tab moves from cell to cell, and in the last cell it adds a new row.

quiz.question: Which Excel list is best prepared for a mail merge?
options: One client per column, with the names going across
Headings in row 1, one client per row, no blank rows
Clients split into separate sheets by city with no headings
All details for each client typed into a single cell
quiz.explanation: Word reads the first row as field names and each row below as one record.

quiz.question: What is the right order of the main buttons on the Mailings tab for a letter merge?
options: Select Recipients, Finish & Merge, Insert Merge Field, Start Mail Merge, Preview Results
Start Mail Merge, Select Recipients, Insert Merge Field, Preview Results, Finish & Merge
Insert Merge Field, Start Mail Merge, Finish & Merge, Select Recipients, Preview Results
Preview Results, Select Recipients, Start Mail Merge, Finish & Merge, Insert Merge Field
quiz.explanation: You choose the document type, link the list, place fields, check the results, then complete the merge.

quiz.question: Which shortcut turns Track Changes on or off in Word for Windows?
options: Ctrl + Shift + T
Ctrl + Shift + E
Ctrl + T
Ctrl + Alt + Shift + T
quiz.explanation: Ctrl + Shift + E toggles Track Changes. You can also use Review > Track Changes.

quiz.question: A document is set to No Markup view and looks clean. Is it safe to send to a client?
options: Yes; No Markup view removes all tracked changes and comments permanently
Yes, as long as the file is saved first
Not yet; the tracked changes and comments are still in the file
Only if Track Changes is also switched on
quiz.explanation: No Markup is a view setting. The changes remain and the client can display them. Accept or reject them and delete comments first.

quiz.question: Which shortcut inserts a new comment in Word for Windows?
options: Ctrl + M
Ctrl + Alt + M
Ctrl + Shift + M
Alt + C
quiz.explanation: Ctrl + Alt + M inserts a comment. Ctrl + M indents a paragraph in Word.

quiz.question: A 6-page staff list table should show its column headings at the top of every page. What should Bilal use?
options: Repeat Header Rows on the table's top row
Copy the header row and paste it on each page
Put the headings in the page header instead
Insert a page break after every 20 rows
quiz.explanation: Repeat Header Rows makes Word show the first row on each new page automatically, even when rows are added.

quiz.question: Before e-mailing a final agreement outside the company, which Word tool helps find hidden comments, tracked changes and personal information?
options: Review > Word Count
File > Info > Check for Issues > Inspect Document
Home > Clear All Formatting
View > Read Mode
quiz.explanation: Inspect Document checks for hidden content and lets you remove it. Menu names can differ slightly between versions.

sessions.title: Advanced Excel: IF, VLOOKUP and XLOOKUP, Filters, PivotTables and Conditional Formatting
sessions.summary: Make Excel decide with IF, fetch prices with VLOOKUP and XLOOKUP, lock references with $, focus data with sorting and filtering, summarise thousands of rows with PivotTables, and highlight results with conditional formatting.
objectives: Write IF and nested IF formulas and use absolute references
Look up values with VLOOKUP (exact match) and XLOOKUP, and handle errors
Sort and filter data and build and refresh a PivotTable
Apply conditional formatting that is clear to every reader

cards.title: Three branches, one messy sheet
cards.setting: Rashid Fabrics now has three branches in Faisalabad. Monday morning, 2,000 rows of sales on the screen.

lines.text: Ayesha beti, I have 2,000 rows of sales from three branches. Which salesman met his target? Which fabric sells best where? I am drowning.
Uncle, the answers are already in your sheet. We just need the right tools to ask the questions.
Four tools will do it: IF to decide, a lookup to fetch prices, filters to focus, and a PivotTable to summarise.
Last week my manager used VLOOKUP and it showed the wrong price for half the items.
That usually means one missing word in the formula. We will find it together.
And I will colour the targets green and red, so you see the winners at a glance.

scenes.heading: The question
scenes.narration: IF asks a yes-or-no question about a cell. Did the salesman sell at least 100,000 rupees? The question is called the logical test, for example C2>=100000.

scenes.heading: If the answer is yes
scenes.narration: The second part is what Excel shows when the test is true, for example "Target met". Text must go inside double quotes.

scenes.heading: If the answer is no
scenes.narration: The third part is shown when the test is false, for example "Below target". The full formula is =IF(C2>=100000,"Target met","Below target").

scenes.heading: More than two answers
scenes.narration: You can put one IF inside another: =IF(C2>=150000,"Star",IF(C2>=100000,"Met","Below")). Excel checks from the first test to the last.

scenes.heading: Commas or semicolons
scenes.narration: Some Windows region settings make Excel use semicolons between arguments instead of commas. If Excel rejects a comma, try a semicolon.

cards.title: Fixed cells with the $ sign
cards.body:
When you copy a formula down, Excel moves its cell references with it. That is usually what you want. But sometimes one cell should stay fixed, such as a target in F1.

- `=C2>=F1` copied down becomes `=C3>=F2`, `=C4>=F3`... wrong.
- `=C2>=$F$1` copied down becomes `=C3>=$F$1`, `=C4>=$F$1`... right.

The `$` locks the column and row. Click on the reference in the formula and press **F4** to add the dollar signs; press F4 again to cycle through `F$1`, `$F1` and back to `F1`.

cards.question: Target is in F1. Ayesha writes =IF(C2>=$F$1,"Met","Below") in D2 and copies it down to D3. What is in D3?
options: =IF(C3>=$F$1,"Met","Below")
=IF(C2>=$F$1,"Met","Below")
=IF(C3>=$F$2,"Met","Below")
=IF(C3>=F2,"Met","Below")
cards.explanation: The relative reference C2 moves down to C3. The absolute reference $F$1 stays locked on the target.

cards.title: VLOOKUP vs XLOOKUP
cards.caption: Both fetch a value from a list, such as a price for an item code. XLOOKUP is newer and simpler, but not every version has it.

items.label: Example
items.left: =VLOOKUP(A2,Prices!A:C,3,FALSE)
items.right: =XLOOKUP(A2,Prices!A:A,Prices!C:C,"Not found")

items.label: Where it looks
items.left: Only in the first column of the table you give it
items.right: In any column you choose

items.label: What it returns
items.left: A column to the right, chosen by number (3 = third column)
items.right: Any column you choose, left or right

items.label: Exact match
items.left: Must add FALSE (or 0) as the last argument
items.right: Exact match is the default

items.label: Not found
items.left: Shows #N/A unless wrapped in IFERROR
items.right: Can show your own message with the fourth argument

items.label: Available in
items.left: Almost every Excel version
items.right: Microsoft 365 and Excel 2021 or later

cards.title: The wrong prices
cards.situation: Rashid's manager used =VLOOKUP(A2,Prices!A:C,3) to fetch prices for item codes. Many prices are wrong, but no error shows. The price list is not sorted by code. What is the best fix?

choices.text: Add FALSE as the fourth argument: =VLOOKUP(A2,Prices!A:C,3,FALSE), or use XLOOKUP if their Excel has it, then spot-check a few prices.
choices.outcome: The prices are now right. Without FALSE, VLOOKUP does an approximate match that expects a sorted list, so it quietly picked nearby codes.

choices.text: Sort the price list by item code and keep the formula as it is.
choices.outcome: This may stop most errors, but approximate match can still return a price for a code that is not on the list. Exact match is safer for codes.

choices.text: Change the 3 to a 2 in the formula.
choices.outcome: That only changes which column is returned. It does not fix the approximate matching that caused the problem.

choices.text: Type the prices in by hand from now on.
choices.outcome: With hundreds of items this is slow and brings back typing errors. The formula needs one small fix, not removing.

cards.back: A lookup could not find the value. Check spelling, extra spaces, or whether the code is in the list.
The formula divides by zero or by an empty cell.
The formula expected a number but found text, for example 'Rs 500' typed as text.
The formula points to a cell that was deleted.
Excel does not recognise a name, often a misspelt function like =SUMM, or a function your version does not have.
Shows your own message instead of any error the formula produces.

cards.title: Build a PivotTable
cards.caption: A PivotTable summarises thousands of rows in seconds, without changing your data.

items.label: Clean the data
items.detail: One heading per column, no blank rows or merged cells. Press Ctrl + T to make it a Table.

items.label: Insert PivotTable
items.detail: Click inside the data, then Insert > PivotTable, and choose New Worksheet.

items.label: Drag to Rows
items.detail: Drag Branch into Rows to list each branch once.

items.label: Drag to Columns
items.detail: Drag Fabric into Columns to compare lawn, cotton and silk side by side.

items.label: Drag to Values
items.detail: Drag Amount into Values. Check it says Sum of Amount, not Count.

items.label: Refresh
items.detail: When new sales are added, right-click the PivotTable and choose Refresh.

cards.title: Which formula does the job?
cards.prompt: Match each task to the formula that does it.

pairs.left: Show 'Pass' if B2 is 50 or more, otherwise 'Fail'
pairs.right: =IF(B2>=50,"Pass","Fail")

pairs.left: Find the price for the code in A2 from columns A to C
pairs.right: =VLOOKUP(A2,Prices!A:C,3,FALSE)

pairs.left: Find the price and show 'Missing' if the code is not found
pairs.right: =XLOOKUP(A2,Prices!A:A,Prices!C:C,"Missing")

pairs.left: Count how many sales rows are from Madina Town
pairs.right: =COUNTIF(B:B,"Madina Town")

pairs.left: Add up all sales from Madina Town
pairs.right: =SUMIF(B:B,"Madina Town",C:C)

cards.title: Sort, filter and conditional formatting
cards.body:
- **Sort** puts rows in order: Data > Sort. Select the whole table first (or use a Table) so each row stays together.
- **Filter** hides rows you do not need right now: **Ctrl + Shift + L** adds or removes the filter arrows. Filtered rows are hidden, not deleted.
- **Conditional formatting** colours cells by rule: Home > Conditional Formatting. Use Highlight Cells Rules for 'greater than', or Data Bars and Color Scales to see patterns.
- Use colour with meaning and a short note: green = target met, red = below. Some people cannot tell red from green, so add a word or icon too.

cards.title: Sort, filter, PivotTable or conditional formatting?
cards.prompt: Choose the best tool for each of Rashid's questions.

items.text: Show only one branch's rows for checking
List sales from biggest to smallest
Total sales for each branch by each fabric type
Monthly totals per salesman from 2,000 rows
Make any sale above Rs 50,000 turn green automatically
Show shaded bars inside cells to compare targets at a glance

cards.title: Rashid's Monday dashboard
cards.body:
Ayesha builds one sheet that Rashid opens every Monday:

- A Table of all sales, filtered to last week with one click.
- A column `Status` with `=IF(C2>=$F$1,"Met","Below")`, coloured green or red by conditional formatting.
- A `Price` column using XLOOKUP from the price list sheet, showing "Check code" if an item is missing.
- A PivotTable: branches in rows, fabrics in columns, Sum of Amount in values, refreshed after new data is pasted in.

Rashid now spots the slowest branch in ten seconds instead of an evening with a calculator.

cards.question: Ayesha's Excel 2016 shows #NAME? when she types an XLOOKUP formula. What is the most likely reason?
options: The lookup value is missing from the list
XLOOKUP is not available in Excel 2016
The column is too narrow to show the result
She forgot to add FALSE at the end
cards.explanation: XLOOKUP is available in Microsoft 365 and Excel 2021 or later. Older versions do not recognise it and show #NAME?. She can use VLOOKUP with FALSE instead.

cards.title: Make data easy for every tool
cards.body:
- Press **Ctrl + T** to turn a range into a Table. Formulas, filters and PivotTables then grow automatically with new rows.
- **View > Freeze Panes > Freeze Top Row** keeps headings visible while you scroll.
- Keep one type of data per column: dates in one, branch names in another, amounts as plain numbers.

Menus and button names can differ between Office versions (for example Microsoft 365, Office 2021 or Office 2016), so if a button has moved, use the search box at the top of the window.

cards.title: Take-aways from the Data Bazaar
items: =IF(test, value if true, value if false) lets Excel decide; text answers go in double quotes.
Lock a fixed cell with $ (press F4) so it does not move when you copy a formula, e.g. $F$1.
VLOOKUP looks in the first column and needs FALSE for an exact match; XLOOKUP is exact by default but needs Microsoft 365 or Excel 2021+.
Sort and filter (Ctrl + Shift + L) focus the data; filtering hides rows, it does not delete them.
PivotTables summarise thousands of rows by dragging fields to Rows, Columns and Values; refresh after new data.
Conditional formatting colours cells by rule; add a word too, because not everyone sees red and green.

cards.prompt: Think of a list you or your workplace keeps: fees, stock, orders or attendance. Write one question you would answer with IF, one with a lookup and one with a PivotTable.

quiz.question: C2 holds 120000. What does =IF(C2>=100000,"Met","Below") show?
options: Met
Below
TRUE
quiz.explanation: The test 120000 >= 100000 is true, so IF returns the second argument, "Met".

quiz.question: Which is a correctly written IF formula in Excel?
options: =IF(B2>=50,"Pass","Fail")
=IF(B2>=50,Pass,Fail)
=IF B2>=50 THEN "Pass" ELSE "Fail"
=IF("Pass",B2>=50,"Fail")
quiz.explanation: The test comes first, then the true value, then the false value. Text must be inside double quotes, otherwise Excel shows #NAME?.

quiz.question: In =VLOOKUP(A2,Prices!A:D,4,FALSE), what does the 4 mean?
options: Look for the value in the fourth row
Allow up to four wrong matches
Search only the first four rows of the price list table
Return the value from the fourth column of the range
quiz.explanation: The third argument of VLOOKUP is the column number within the table range, counting from its first column.

quiz.question: Why should you usually put FALSE at the end of a VLOOKUP for item codes?
options: It makes the formula run faster on large sheets
It hides #N/A errors when a code is missing
It lets VLOOKUP look to the left of the first column
It forces an exact match instead of an approximate one
quiz.explanation: Without FALSE (or 0), VLOOKUP uses approximate match, which assumes sorted data and can return the wrong row without any error.

quiz.question: Which statement about XLOOKUP is correct?
options: It works in every Excel version since 2010
It needs the list sorted in ascending order
It can only search the first column of a table
It can return a column to the left of the lookup column
quiz.explanation: XLOOKUP uses separate lookup and return ranges, so the return column can be anywhere. It needs Microsoft 365 or Excel 2021 or later.

quiz.question: Target is in F1. A formula in D2 is =C2>=F1. After copying it down, rows below give wrong results. What is the fix?
options: Change C2 to $C$2 so the sales stay fixed
Type the formula again in every single row by hand
Sort the column so the target moves to F2
Change F1 to $F$1 so the target stays fixed
quiz.explanation: F1 needs to be absolute ($F$1). C2 must stay relative so each row checks its own sales.

quiz.question: Which keyboard shortcut adds or removes filter arrows on a data range in Excel for Windows?
options: Ctrl + Shift + F
Ctrl + L
Ctrl + Shift + Alt + F
Ctrl + Shift + L
quiz.explanation: Ctrl + Shift + L toggles the filter. Ctrl + L (like Ctrl + T) opens the Create Table box.

quiz.question: A lookup formula shows #N/A. Which is the most likely cause?
options: A cell somewhere in the formula was deleted
The formula divides a number by zero
The value being looked up was not found in the list
The column is too narrow to display the answer
quiz.explanation: #N/A means 'not available': the lookup could not find a match. #REF! is a deleted reference, #DIV/0! is divide by zero, and ##### means a narrow column.

quiz.question: Rashid adds 300 new sales rows to the data behind his PivotTable. The totals do not change. What should he do?
options: Delete the PivotTable and conditional formatting
Press Ctrl + Z to undo the new rows
Right-click the PivotTable and choose Refresh
Sort the data from largest to smallest
quiz.explanation: PivotTables do not update by themselves when source data changes. Refresh them. If the data is an Excel Table, new rows are included in the range.

quiz.question: Which tool would make every sale above Rs 50,000 turn green automatically?
options: A PivotTable
Freeze Panes
Find and Replace
Conditional formatting
quiz.explanation: Conditional formatting applies colours by rule and updates as values change.

sessions.title: Professional Presentations and Productivity: Design, Presenter View, Cloud Sharing and E-mail
sessions.summary: Design slides that persuade, present confidently with Presenter View, share and co-author one cloud copy with Version History, and write professional e-mails with the right use of To, Cc, Bcc and Reply All.
objectives: Design clear, consistent slides using themes and the Slide Master
Deliver a presentation with Presenter View, notes, timer and show shortcuts
Share files safely from OneDrive or SharePoint and use Version History
Write professional e-mails and use To, Cc, Bcc and Reply All correctly

cards.title: The pitch and the Reply All
cards.setting: A youth start-up competition at a hotel in Islamabad. Ayesha's team has 7 minutes to pitch. Bilal is helping from Karachi.

lines.text: Sana Baji, my notes are on paper, my slides have 200 words each, and I am terrified I will forget the numbers.
Presenter View will put your notes and a timer on your laptop while the audience sees only your slides.
I am so sorry. I e-mailed our team's budget file as an attachment, then fixed a mistake, and now there are four versions going around.
One shared file in the cloud, everyone edits the same copy, and version history keeps the old ones. No more 'final-v4'.
And last night I nearly pressed Reply All to complain about the judges' schedule...
Then today is your last stage: slides that persuade, files that stay in one place and e-mails you will never regret sending.

scenes.heading: Two screens, two views
scenes.narration: Connect your laptop to a projector or big screen. In Presenter View the audience sees only the current slide, while your laptop shows the slide, your notes and the next slide.

scenes.heading: Timer and clock
scenes.narration: A timer starts when the show starts, so you can see if you are running over your seven minutes. You can pause or reset it.

scenes.heading: Speaker notes
scenes.narration: Type notes in the Notes pane under each slide while you prepare (View > Notes if it is hidden). Keep them short: key numbers and the next sentence.

scenes.heading: Starting it
scenes.narration: On the Slide Show tab, tick Use Presenter View, then start with F5, or press Alt + F5 to start in Presenter View straight away. You can practise this way even with one screen.

scenes.heading: Useful keys during the show
scenes.narration: Press B for a black screen (to pause and talk), W for white, a slide number then Enter to jump to that slide, and Esc to end.

cards.title: Design slides that persuade
cards.caption: Common guidelines that work for most business talks. Your organisation may have its own template.

items.label: One message per slide
items.detail: Write the heading as a short sentence that states the point.

items.label: Big, few words
items.detail: Text large enough to read from the back; short phrases rather than paragraphs.

items.label: Show, don't list
items.detail: A chart, photo or simple diagram is easier to remember than six bullets.

items.label: Consistent look
items.detail: Use one theme, and set fonts and colours in the Slide Master (View > Slide Master).

items.label: Strong contrast
items.detail: Dark text on a light background or the opposite; avoid busy pictures behind text.

items.label: Check it
items.detail: Run the show from the start, read on a small screen and fix anything hard to read.

cards.back: Start the show from the first slide.
Start from the slide you are on.
Start the show in Presenter View.
Turn the screen black; press again to return.
Turn the screen white; press again to return.
Jump to that slide, e.g. 5 then Enter.
End the slide show.

cards.question: Ayesha is editing slide 6 and wants to rehearse from that slide, not from the start. Which key does that?
options: F5
Ctrl + F5
Shift + F5
Shift + F6
cards.explanation: Shift + F5 starts the show from the current slide; F5 always starts from slide 1.

cards.title: Attachment vs shared cloud link
cards.caption: When several people work on one file, a shared link to one copy in OneDrive or SharePoint usually avoids confusion.

items.label: Copies
items.left: Every e-mail creates a new copy
items.right: One copy that everyone opens

items.label: Edits
items.left: People change different copies
items.right: People can edit at the same time (co-authoring)

items.label: Latest version
items.left: 'Which one is final?'
items.right: Always the file in the cloud; older versions in Version History

items.label: Access
items.left: Anyone the e-mail reaches keeps the file
items.right: You choose who can view or edit, and you can stop sharing later

items.label: Saving
items.left: Manual Ctrl + S
items.right: AutoSave in Microsoft 365 for files stored in OneDrive or SharePoint

cards.title: Sharing and collaborating safely
cards.body:
Save the file to **OneDrive** or your organisation's **SharePoint** or Teams site, then click **Share** at the top right of Word, Excel or PowerPoint.

- Choose **who** gets the link (specific people is safest) and whether they **can edit** or **can only view**. The options available depend on your organisation's settings.
- Use **@mentions** in comments to ask a teammate a question.
- **File > Info > Version History** (or the file name at the top) lets you open or restore an earlier version.
- Never share files with salaries, CNIC numbers or customer data using a link that 'anyone' can open. If you shared the wrong file, go to **Manage Access** and stop sharing.

cards.title: E-mail fields and their jobs
cards.prompt: Match each part of an e-mail to its proper use.

pairs.right: The people who must read and act on the message
People who need to know, but are not expected to act
Hidden recipients, such as customers who should not see each other's addresses
A short, specific summary, e.g. 'Budget v2 for review by Thursday'

pairs.left: Reply All (Ctrl + Shift + R in Outlook)
pairs.right: Answers everyone on the message, so use it only when all of them need your reply
Answers only the sender

cards.title: Write a professional e-mail
cards.prompt: Put the parts of Bilal's e-mail to the competition organisers in order.
steps: A clear subject: 'Team Indus: question about pitch slot on 6 Dec'
A greeting with the person's name: 'Dear Mr Kamran,'
The purpose in the first line: 'Could our slot move from 9:00 to 11:00?'
One or two lines of reason and any detail they need
A polite close with what happens next: 'Thank you; please let me know by Tuesday.'
Your name, team and phone number, then a check of To, Cc and attachments before Send

cards.title: Professional or risky e-mail habit?
cards.prompt: Sort each e-mail habit.

items.text: Putting the request in the first two lines
Using Bcc when e-mailing 60 customers who do not know each other
Reading the message again before pressing Send when you feel angry
Sharing a OneDrive link set to specific people instead of attaching a confidential file
Pressing Reply All to a 200-person message to say 'Thanks'
A subject line that just says 'Hi' or 'Urgent!!!'
Writing the whole message in CAPITAL LETTERS
Forwarding a long thread with private salary details to an outside supplier

cards.title: The angry Reply All
cards.situation: At 11 p.m. the organisers e-mail all 40 teams and 6 judges: the pitch order has changed and Ayesha's team now goes first at 8:30 a.m. Bilal is upset and types a long reply about 'unfair, last-minute planning', with his cursor on Reply All. What should he do?

choices.text: Save it as a draft, sleep, and next morning send a short, polite Reply only to the organiser asking if a later slot is possible.
choices.outcome: The organiser moves them to 10:00 because another team asked to go early. Bilal kept his reputation and got what the team needed.

choices.text: Delete the e-mail and say nothing at all.
choices.outcome: No harm is done, but the team loses the chance to ask politely for a better slot.

choices.text: Send it to everyone so the other teams support his complaint.
choices.outcome: Forty-five people now see an angry message from Team Indus, including the judges. Once sent, it cannot be reliably taken back.

choices.text: Send it to the organiser only, as written, right now.
choices.outcome: Better than Reply All, but an angry late-night message still harms the relationship. Calm wording would work better.

cards.title: Ayesha's pitch, rebuilt
cards.body:
Ayesha cut her 14 slides to 7. Each heading now says the point, such as 'Small shops lose stock to counting errors every week', backed by her own survey of 20 shops in Lahore, which she explains out loud. Slide 4 is one chart instead of a table. Her notes hold only the numbers and her next line.

She practised three times with Presenter View and the timer, finishing at 6 minutes 20 seconds. When a judge asked about costs, she typed 9 and pressed Enter to jump straight to her backup slide.

cards.question: Bilal must send a newsletter to 80 shop owners who do not know each other. Where should their addresses go?
options: All in To, so everyone feels included
All in Cc, so they can reply to each other
In the Subject line, separated by commas
In Bcc, with his own address in To
cards.explanation: Bcc hides each address from the others, protecting their privacy. Putting 80 strangers in To or Cc shares everyone's e-mail address with everyone.

cards.title: Productivity habits for the office
cards.body:
- Keep work files in OneDrive or SharePoint so they are backed up and available on other devices.
- In Outlook, use **flags** or **categories** for e-mails you must act on, and turn big tasks into calendar blocks.
- Use **@mentions** and comments in shared files instead of long e-mail threads.
- Check your organisation's rules before sharing any file outside it.

Menus and button names can differ between Office versions (for example Microsoft 365, Office 2021 or Office 2016), so if a button has moved, use the search box at the top of the window.
